request.spec:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button on each person's row downloads their row as a CSV file: a header line cell,value then one
line per cell for person-name, person-grade, person-claimed, person-due-total, person-statement-count,
person-overdue-total, person-hold, person-retired, person-aliases and person-score, in that order,
each with the value as the row shows it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now has a **Row (CSV)** button (`data-testid="person-export"`) that downloads the row as a CSV file. The file starts with a `cell,value` header, followed by one line for each of the ten cells in the order you listed. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the export test and the three other scenarios.

The change is front end only, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people-list.ts`:
- **The button** is in the row's actions, next to the existing "Statement (CSV)" button.
- **The new `exportPersonCsv(p)` method** works out each value with the same functions the row's cells use, and passes figures through the same locale formatting. A value like `Lee, Jo (B)` gets quoted by the existing `downloadCsv` helper.

Because the method computes the values instead of copying them off the page, the CSV still has all ten values when some of those columns are hidden. The test doesn't hide any columns, so that case hasn't been run.

No server or database change was needed, and the tests don't expect an audit record for an export, so none is written.
